_comment: WHAT EACH CORPUS FILE IS FOR. Read by BOTH WishCorpus (Java) and the tools/ scripts (Python), because roles that live in two places drift -- which is exactly how the wish classifier ended up reading its own output, and how creatures.jsonl sat unloaded for months while nothing noticed.

roles.RUNNABLE: Cases with a spec that the stress loop executes. They prove the engine works. A case we can already run does NOT get to vote on what to build next -- that is coverage, not demand.
roles.GAPS: Wishes he made that the engine CANNOT express. The roadmap signal, and the one thing no commit-reading tool can ever produce: a commit is evidence of something we DID build, so absences are invisible to it.
roles.DEMAND_DIRECT: Sentences a child actually typed. The only direct evidence in the corpus.
roles.DEMAND_HISTORICAL: Features he asked for that we DID build, mined from a mod repo. Three jobs: how his interests shift over time, how far we have got, and a regression corpus -- a thing we built once should keep working.
roles.CALIBRATION: Real agent OUTPUT, kept to calibrate a gate. Not a wish; never counted as demand in either direction.
roles.PANEL: A fixed, VERSIONED denominator: the wishes a layer is measured on. Not demand and not a fixture -- a panel exists so a quality number is always 'level-3 at panel v<N>' and a silent edit to the wish list cannot move a trend line. Never counted as demand.

files.note: Hand-curated. Its `unsupported` cases are the 119 gaps; the rest carry specs and run. Preserves his spelling -- bild, drorbridge, ginormus -- which the commit miner cannot.
PRIVATE: the rows of wishes.jsonl whose prompt is a child's own sentence. Same schema, loaded beside it; the public cut has no copy and loads without it.
Generated by tools/gen-picture-corpus.py: pictures hung as map art on a real wall, and the three caps that must be said.
The creature eval prompts. Sat outside the loader for its whole life because it carries tier/sourcing rather than the shared schema.
PRIVATE: the rows of creatures.jsonl whose prompt is a child's own sentence (or near enough). Same schema; CreatureCorpus unions it in after creatures.jsonl, and the public cut runs without it.
kind=demand: no spec, nothing to run, counted only. Re-mine after a play session and it grows.
kind=demand. Carries a date, so trends are sliceable. Also the promotion queue: give one a spec and it becomes RUNNABLE regression coverage.
Agent output. Gates on the unit suite via RealBuildCalibrationTest, not here -- one of these plans is 192,000 blocks.

The agent's real TOOL CALLS, mined by tools/mine-tool-calls.py. Answers 'what did the agent actually do' -- the question ten open issues are blocked on and the one the raw log cannot answer durably, because it is machine-local and dies with the container. test:true gate traffic is excluded; args and result are dropped (args is clipped mid-value, which is how 'the agent never uses palette' got believed). Unlike every other CALIBRATION file this one calibrates REPORTS rather than a gate, and it MERGES rather than being rebuilt, so two machines folding in either order agree.
NOT wishes: 154 CBScript COMPILE RECORDS, regression fixtures for the compiler. Declared so no ranking ever counts them again.

THE PUBLIC SAFETY SET (docs/CHILD_SAFETY_PLAN.md section 10), version 3: 974 labelled requests a child-safety grader must block, redirect (LIKELY) or allow (FINE/MAYBE). Rows are GENERATED (written for the objectionable cells of the four axes, for the near-misses that must still be granted, and to give every band enough `allow` rows to measure a false-positive rate) or WISHED from bol-wishes.jsonl and wishes.jsonl (band keyword-assigned, and every such row says so in `why`). No row a child typed is here: since v3 the 84 real wishes, 4 mined rows with the same words and 3 generated rows using a family member's name are a PRIVATE held-out set (corpus/safety-heldout.jsonl), never published. loadIntoStress is false: there is no spec to run, kind=safety has no StressHarness, and it gates through tools/safety-arm.py. VERSIONED: a row is never reworded -- retire it with a reason, add a new id, bump corpusVersion -- because corpus/safety-floor.json records a floor per corpus version and refuses to compare across one.

_repoFilesComment: `files` above is the SHIPPED corpus, under src/main/resources/corpus/, and CorpusManifestTest asserts every entry resolves as a classpath resource. `repoFiles` is for corpus data that lives in the repo-root corpus/ tree and is read by tools rather than by the mod -- declared here so its role is stated in the one place roles live, and kept in a separate list so the resource check keeps meaning what it says.

repoFiles.note: The safety arm's floors (docs/CHILD_SAFETY_PLAN.md section 10 item 3): one row per metric per band per CORPUS VERSION, each a MEASURED value with the n, date and commit that measured it. UNLIKE every other floor in this repo the FPR rows run DOWNWARDS -- a false-positive rate is lower-is-better, so the floor is the Wilson UPPER bound and tools/safety-arm.py --check fails when the measured rate EXCEEDS it; blocked_recall is the usual direction (Wilson LOWER bound, fails when it falls below). A mismatched corpus version is reported, never compared, and a row with no value cannot slip (exit 3, UNMEASURED, never exit 1). Every row ships as BASELINE: CS-S1b measures them.

One directory per tools/safety-arm.py run: conditions.json (what was graded, with which prompt sha, schema sha and model), results.jsonl (one line per corpus row per repeat, carrying the raw model reply so a verdict can be re-read without re-running the grader), report.md, and the tools/evalrun.py run record + score rows so trend.py reads it for free. Committed for a run whose numbers a floor is set from; a scratch run is not. The sibling cache corpus/safety-arm-cache/ is keyed on (prompt sha, schema sha, model, text sha, repeat index) -- committing it is what makes a report reproducible on a machine with no CLI.
